title: Directed colimit of a directed system of abelian groups
statement: Let $(I,\leq)$ be a nonempty directed set (any two elements have a common upper bound). A *directed system of abelian groups* indexed by $I$ is a family of abelian groups $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ with homomorphisms $f_{ij}:G_i\to G_j$ for $i\leq j$ such that $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{jk}\circ f_{ij}=f_{ik}$ for $i\leq j\leq k$. Its *directed colimit* (direct limit) $\varinjlim_{i\in I}G_i$ is the abelian group $\bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}G_i\bigr)/N$, where $N$ is the subgroup generated by the elements $x-f_{ij}(x)$ for $i\leq j$ and $x\in G_i$, together with the canonical homomorphisms $\iota_i:G_i\to\varinjlim G_i$, which satisfy $\iota_j\circ f_{ij}=\iota_i$. Concretely: every element of $\varinjlim G_i$ is $\iota_i(x)$ for some $i$ and some $x\in G_i$ (a *representative at the stage $i$*), and $\iota_i(x)=\iota_j(y)$ holds if and only if there is $k\geq i,j$ with $f_{ik}(x)=f_{jk}(y)$ (equality *at a common later stage*); in particular $\iota_i(x)=0$ if and only if $f_{ik}(x)=0$ for some $k\geq i$. The directed colimit has the universal property: for every abelian group $P$ and homomorphisms $g_i:G_i\to P$ with $g_j\circ f_{ij}=g_i$ there is a unique homomorphism $g:\varinjlim G_i\to P$ with $g\circ\iota_i=g_i$.
